entries.lesson_title: Windowing a Signal Over a Time Interval
entries.core_move: Construct a finite-duration version of a continuous-time signal by multiplying it by the shifted-unit-step window $u(t-a)-u(t-b)$ and identifying the interval over which the original signal is retained.
Construct a piecewise constant continuous-time signal by converting its interval-by-interval level changes into a sum of scaled shifted unit steps.
Construct a piecewise linear continuous-time signal by converting each breakpoint's slope change into a shifted ramp term gated by unit steps.
Construct a finite-duration triangular signal from its rise, peak, fall, and zero regions using shifted linear segments gated by unit steps.
Simplify overlapping shifted-unit-step expressions by identifying their active time intervals and combining like signal segments into an equivalent compact expression.

entries.lesson_title: Converting Graphs into Unit Step Expressions
entries.core_move: Translate a continuous-time signal graph into a simplified unit step expression by identifying its breakpoints, interval formulas, and shifted unit-step windows.
